newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec sees C$245 mln 1996/97 revenue shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Quebec sees C$245 mln 1996/97 revenue shortfall.

text.p: Quebec Finance Minister Bernard Landry said on Thursday that a revision of the government's revenue and expediture forecasts shows a budget shortfall of C$245 million compared with forecasts made in its May 9 budget.
The shortfall stems from the downward adjustment to the government's own-source revenue forecast, Landry said.
The minister said Quebec reaffirmed its deficit objective of C$3.275 billion for fiscal 1996/97, which ends March 31.
"The deficit target of C$3.275 billion for 1996/97 set in the budget speech must be achieved," Landry told reporters.

Landry said the adjustment to Quebec's own-source revenue forecast is attributable mainly to the revised economic outlook, the lower-than-expected tax yield from the elimination of the C$100,000 lifetime capital gains exemption and the reduced yield of the Quebec sales tax.

He said the C$245 million revenue shortfall would be made up through measures taken to increase the earnings of government corporations by C$50 million and additional savings of C$195 million in program spending for the year.
Quebec's revised forecast shows shortfalls of C$493 million in 1997/98, C$292 million in 1998/99 and C$379 million in 1999/2000, compared to forecasts made in the May 9 budget.
"The measures required to achieve the deficit objectives for the years 1997/98 to 1999/2000 will be announced next spring when the estimates and the budget speech are tabled," Landry said.

He said possible solutions include a further reduction in program spending, improving the results of government corporations, intensifying efforts to collect government revenues, and a review of tax expenditures and fees.
Landry said Quebec reaffirmed its commitment to reduce the deficit to C$2.2 billion in 1997/98, C$1.2 billion in 1998/99 and zero in 1999/2000.
Quebec's revised forecasts are based on growth in real gross domestic product for the province of 1.3 percent and an annual inflation rate of 1.8 percent in calendar 1997.
